subject: Slate fallout: ownership, containment, and escalation notes
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Grant <alyssa.grant@healthco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Slate fallout: containment proposal and decision needed by EOD Mon

Alyssa — thanks for the quick sync this morning. Per our call, HealthCo's procurement hold on the signing packet threatens the close date we committed to in the MAP (attached). I want to capture the immediate containment options so we can be explicit with execs tomorrow.

Summary of risk (short):
- Procurement requires a final SOC2 evidence bundle + a countersigned SLA addendum; they will not start routing paperwork until both are in the folder.
- That gating item is estimated to add 7–12 business days based on HealthCo procurement cadence.
- If that slip occurs, the planned evaluation window for the pilot (10/18–10/25) will be delayed and will push go-live into November, affecting onboarding and assigned support slots.

Containment options (recommendation first):
1) Conditional pilot kick: sign an interim confidentiality & limited-scope MOU (1–2 pages) to allow model ingestion and early eval while procurement finalizes the full contract. This preserves the evaluation dates.
2) Exec credit and compressed evaluation: provide a temporary 10% credit on month 1 and run a focused 3-day evaluation for core workflows only.
3) Full hold and formal replan: accept a slip, reissue MAP with new milestones and a hard checkpoint for 11/8.

Ask: can HealthCo confirm which route they prefer by EOD Monday (10/12)? If option 1, we will send the MOU draft and a short data handling checklist for your procurement team.

I've attached the current MAP (HealthCo_MAP_v3.xlsx) and a draft MOU template.

Thanks — Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Director, GTM Programs
Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0189
Attachments: HealthCo_MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), draft_MOU.docx (attachment stub)

From: Alyssa Grant <alyssa.grant@healthco.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@healthco.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Slate fallout: containment proposal and decision needed by EOD Mon

Hannah — appreciate the clear summary. Quick responses from procurement side:
- We do need the SOC2 evidence bundle (can accept a packaged zip) and the countersigned SLA addendum before legal will clear the final signature.
- Our procurement lead estimates 7–10 business days once they have those two items, assuming no additional redlines.

That said, we are motivated to keep the evaluation window if possible. Two follow-ups:
1) Can Redwood accept the MOU approach (option 1)? Procurement will still require the SOC2 bundle but would accept a limited-scope MOU to allow our infra team to start ingestion.
2) If we go with the MOU, we need the data handling checklist ASAP and a short statement of security controls for the evaluation environment.

I'll loop legal/procurement into the thread so we can move quickly.

—Alyssa

Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 14:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: short-term containment ask + exec approval request

Team — looped Marissa as this has a hard exec impact if the evaluation window slips. Short request for Marissa/execs:
- Ask 1: Approve issuing a 10% month-1 credit and sign the limited-scope MOU to preserve evaluation dates (option 1 + credit).
- Ask 2: Authorize a temporary SLA exception (see attached SLA-exception-approval.pdf) enabling a controlled evaluation environment pending countersignature.

If approved, action plan:
1) Ben to draft and send the MOU (today).
2) Laura to assemble and verify SOC2 evidence bundle and upload to HealthCo procurement portal (by EOD Tue 10/13).
3) Marissa to approve credit + SLA exception (need confirmation email).

Why this matters: losing the planned eval window pushes onboarding resources and delays revenue recognition by ~4 weeks; preserves seat assignments and reduces churn risk.

Please reply with approvals or concerns.

Thanks — Hannah

Attachments: SLA-exception-approval.pdf (stub)
